items.title: What Happens if I Don't File a Nil T2?
items.desc: The tax year stays open and the Canada Revenue Agency can demand the return and assess the corporation arbitrarily.
items.kw: what happens if i dont file a nil t2

items.title: What Happens if I Don't File My T2 for Five Years?
items.desc: All five returns stay outstanding and each year is filed separately. Filing all five at once is routine and closes the years in a single pass.
items.kw: what happens if i dont file my t2 for five years

items.title: What Happens if I Don't File a T2 Before Dissolving?
items.desc: Dissolution can be held up and the outstanding years remain owed. An unfiled year blocks the clearance certificate that lets a corporation close.
items.kw: what happens if i dont file a t2 before dissolving

items.title: What Happens if a Dormant Corporation Is Not Reported?
items.desc: There is no separate dormancy filing, so the obligation is simply the annual T2. Telling the CRA a corporation is inactive does not replace it.
items.kw: what happens if a dormant corporation is not reported

items.title: What Happens if I Ignore a CRA Demand to File a T2?
items.desc: The Canada Revenue Agency can assess the corporation arbitrarily, without waiting for the return. Filing the real return replaces that assessment.
items.kw: what happens if i ignore a cra demand to file a t2

items.title: What Happens if a Numbered Company Does Not File?
items.desc: Nothing changes because the corporation has a number instead of a name. A numbered company files a T2 within six months of each fiscal year-end.
items.kw: what happens if a numbered company does not file

items.title: What Happens if I Don't File After Dissolution?
items.desc: The final return is still required and the years before dissolution stay outstanding. Dissolving does not close earlier years or cancel the returns.
items.kw: what happens if i dont file after dissolution

items.title: Do I Need to File a T2 if My Corporation Had No Activity?
items.desc: Yes. Every resident corporation must file a T2 return within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved.
items.kw: do i need to file a t2 if my corporation had no activity

items.title: Do I Need to File a Nil T2 With No Bank Account?
items.desc: Yes. The T2 obligation follows the corporation's existence, not its banking, so a return is due within six months of each fiscal year-end regardless.
items.kw: do i need to file a nil t2 with no bank account

items.title: Do I Need Financial Statements for a Nil T2 Return?
items.desc: No audited or reviewed statements are needed, but the return still carries GIFI schedules showing zero.
items.kw: do i need financial statements for a nil t2 return

items.title: Do I Need to File a T2 for the Year of Dissolution?
items.desc: Yes. A final T2 covers the period from the start of that fiscal year to the dissolution date, and it is due within six months of dissolution.
items.kw: do i need to file a t2 for the year of dissolution

items.title: Do I Need a Business Number to File a Nil T2?
items.desc: Yes. The return is filed against the corporation's nine-digit business number and its corporation income tax account, so the number must exist.
items.kw: do i need a business number to file a nil t2

items.title: Do I Need to File a Nil T2 if I Never Started Operating?
items.desc: Yes. The first tax year begins on the incorporation date, not the day trading starts, so a return is due six months after that first year-end.
items.kw: do i need to file a nil t2 if i never started operating

items.title: Do I Need to File a T2 Every Year When Inactive?
items.desc: Yes, every year. Inactive is a description, not a filing status, so a T2 falls due six months after each year-end until the corporation is closed.
items.kw: do i need to file a t2 every year when inactive

items.title: Can I File Five Years of Nil T2 Returns at Once?
items.desc: Yes. Five missed fiscal year-ends mean five separate returns, and all five can be prepared and transmitted in one pass.
items.kw: can i file five years of nil t2 returns at once

items.title: Can I File a Nil T2 Myself Without an Accountant?
items.desc: Yes. Nothing requires a corporation to use an accountant. A corporation that engages an electronic filer signs Form T183CORP before transmission.
items.kw: can i file a nil t2 myself without an accountant

items.title: Can I Dissolve My Corporation With Unfiled T2 Returns?
items.desc: Not cleanly. The corporate registry and the Canada Revenue Agency are separate, so a registry may strike a corporation while its tax years remain outstanding.
items.kw: can i dissolve my corporation with unfiled t2 returns

items.title: Can I File a Nil T2 Late Without a Penalty?
items.desc: What actually applies to a late nil T2: the percentage penalty, the year that stays open, a demand to file, and the non-resident per-day charge.
items.kw: can i file a nil t2 late without a penalty

items.title: Can I File Nil T2 Returns for a Corporation I Forgot About?
items.desc: Yes. A corporation left alone still has a fiscal year-end for every year since incorporation, and each of those years can be filed now.
items.kw: can i file nil t2 returns for a corporation i forgot about

items.title: Can I Still File a T2 After My Corporation Was Dissolved?
items.desc: Yes. A final return is due within six months of the dissolution date, and years left unfiled before dissolution can still be filed afterwards.
items.kw: can i still file a t2 after my corporation was dissolved

items.title: Can I Catch Up on Unfiled T2 Returns Without an Audit?
items.desc: Catching up is an ordinary filing, not an audit. Each outstanding year is filed as its own T2 return and assessed in the normal way.
items.kw: can i catch up on unfiled t2 returns without an audit

items.title: How Do I File a Nil T2 Return in Canada?
items.desc: You file a T2 return for the tax year showing no income and no expenses, then transmit it to the Canada Revenue Agency electronically.
items.kw: how do i file a nil t2 return in canada

items.title: How Do I Catch Up on Years of Unfiled T2 Returns?
items.desc: You file one T2 return for each outstanding tax year, oldest first, each with its own fiscal year dates. There is no combined return that covers several years.
items.kw: how do i catch up on years of unfiled t2 returns

items.title: How Do I Know if My Corporation Counts as Dormant?
items.desc: A corporation is treated as dormant for a tax year when it carried on no business, earned nothing and paid nothing out during that year.
items.kw: how do i know if my corporation counts as dormant

items.title: How Do I Find Out Which T2 Years Are Outstanding?
items.desc: Your corporate tax account in the Canada Revenue Agency's My Business Account lists every tax year and whether a return has been assessed.
items.kw: how do i find out which t2 years are outstanding

items.title: How Do I Dissolve a Corporation That Has Never Filed a T2?
items.desc: Every outstanding T2 is filed first, including a final return to the dissolution date, and then dissolution is applied for through the registry.
items.kw: how do i dissolve a corporation that has never filed a t2

items.title: How Do I Close My Corporate Tax Account After Dissolution?
items.desc: The corporate income tax account is closed by asking the Canada Revenue Agency to close the Business Number programme accounts, using Form RC145.
items.kw: how do i close my corporate tax account after dissolution

items.title: How Do I Fix a Nil T2 Filed With the Wrong Year-End?
items.desc: A return filed for the wrong period is corrected by filing for the correct period, because the fiscal year dates are what define which year a return covers.
items.kw: how do i fix a nil t2 filed with the wrong year-end

items.title: When Should I File My First T2 After Incorporating?
items.desc: The first T2 is due within six months of the first fiscal year-end, and the corporation chooses that year-end itself when it files.
items.kw: when should i file my first t2 after incorporating

items.title: When Should I File a Nil T2 for a Short First Tax Year?
items.desc: Within six months of the short year-end, on the same rule as a full year. A short first year is still a complete tax year and needs its own T2.
items.kw: when should i file a nil t2 for a short first tax year
